title: pak::scan_deps() empty results when given file path(s)
description:
Basic reprex is to create a folder with the following files:

`test.R`:
```
library(tidymodels)
```

`test.qmd`:
```
---
format: html
---

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
```
```


The following is the observed behavior when scanning from that directory:
```
> pak::scan_deps()

Dependencies:
+ rmarkdown  @ test.qmd
+ tidymodels @ test.R
+ tidyverse  @ test.qmd
> pak::scan_deps("test.qmd", "./")

> pak::scan_deps("test.R", "./")

> pak::scan_deps(c("test.qmd","test.R"), "./")

```

In previous versions (not sure when this broke) of pak the latter three calls would have returned the file specific dependencies.

title: Installing Packages with pak results in Error for Enterprise Environment
description:
Hi, we would really like to use pak in our secured environment, but with our End-Point Security using pak::pkg_install results in an Error. This is due to the fact that pak is copying installed packages into the TEMP Folder and test-loading them.

This issue is similar to https://github.com/r-lib/pak/issues/293 as Corporate Setups often do not allow Execute-Rights in TEMP-directories.

**Proposed Solution:**
Similar to the package "callr" we suggest to introduce an Env-Variable PAK_NO_TEMP_DLLS that circumvents this behavior and just skips the test-loading of installed packages. This would enable our teams to use pak for secured Environments.

-> See the docs of the variable of callr: [CALLR_NO_TEMP_DLLS](https://github.com/r-lib/callr#environment-variables)

Thanks!
Michael

title: Public GitHub packages fail when pak discovers credentials not authorised for the organisation’s SAML SSO
description:
pak cannot install a public package when it discovers a GitHub credential that is not SAML-authorised for the organisation hosting the repository.

For example:

```R
pak::pak("dfe-analytical-services/dfeshiny")
```
fails with:

```
GitHub error: Resource protected by organization SAML enforcement.
You must grant your OAuth token access to this organization.
```

The repository is public. The same installation succeeds when credential discovery is disabled:

```Shell
printf '[credential]\n helper =\n' > /tmp/gitconfig-no-creds
 
env \
-u GITHUB_PAT \
-u GITHUB_TOKEN \
-u GH_TOKEN \
GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/tmp/gitconfig-no-creds \
Rscript --vanilla -e \
'pak::pak("dfe-analytical-services/dfeshiny")'
```
 # Previous issues

This appears to be the SAML variant of:

[r-lib/pak#504: Unnecessary git authentication for public repositories](https://github.com/r-lib/pak/issues/504), where stale credentials prevent installation of public repositories.
[r-lib/pak#890: pak does not work where devtools::install_github does](https://github.com/r-lib/pak/issues/890), where users with credentials configured for other purposes cannot install public packages.
[r-lib/gh#216](https://github.com/r-lib/gh/issues/216), which reports this exact public-repository/SAML behaviour. gh supports .token = NA_character_ to force anonymous access, but pak does not expose an equivalent.

# Why the existing answers are insufficient

Updating or SSO-authorising the credential is not a general solution. This is a public package intended for external users. Those users may have credentials for unrelated GitHub work and may not be members of the organisation, so they cannot authorise their token for its SAML SSO.

Deleting credentials is also not reasonable installation guidance. It can disrupt access to other repositories and tools.

I understand that silently retrying every failed authenticated request anonymously could hide genuine authentication problems, maybe detect this specific SAML error or add an explicit anonymous mode would avoid that ambiguity.

# Suggested changes

Please provide a supported way to install public GitHub packages without credential discovery, for example:

```R
pak::pak(
"dfe-analytical-services/dfeshiny",
github_auth = "anonymous"
)
```
Alternatively:

expose the equivalent of `gh(..., .token = NA_character_)`;
document a supported per-call or environment-level anonymous mode;
detect the specific SAML-enforcement response and suggest anonymous access when the repository is public.

The current workaround requires users to unset several environment variables and replace their Git credential configuration. That is not suitable for normal installation instructions for a public package.

title: Feature request: dependency cooldown (exclude packages newer than N days)
description:
**Problem**

Supply chain attacks often get caught within days of a malicious release. A cooldown lets users skip versions that are too new. uv supports this with relative durations:

```
uv pip install pandas --exclude-newer "7 days"
```

pak has no equivalent. 

**Current workaround**

```r
pak::repo_add(paste0("PPM@", Sys.Date() - 7))
```

This has gaps:

- It requires Posit Package Manager. Users on plain CRAN mirrors or other repositories get no cooldown.
- If PPM has no snapshot for the date, pak uses the next available one, which can include newer packages than requested.
- You can't set this as an environment variable that could be applied to all sessions or all users on a server.

**Proposal**

Add a setting that excludes any package version published less than N days ago. For example:

```r
options(pkg.exclude_newer = "7 days")
# or
Sys.setenv(PKG_EXCLUDE_NEWER = "7 days")
```

For reference, UV supports more than relative days to a similar syntax could be used: https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/resolution/#reproducible-resolutions

**Why in pak**

People use pak to install R packages. This also lets renv inherit the behaviour when it uses pak.

title: Bug: `pkg_remove()` does not accept a character vector of packages to remove
description:
The `pkg` argument of `pkg_remove()` states that it accepts "A character vector of packages to remove." However, internally, this function calls `pkgdepends:: parse_pkg_ref()`, which only accepts a length one vector (line 204):

https://github.com/r-lib/pak/blob/8109ed4f78128b657a0005fb303dd75f55afcce0/R/package.R#L193-L207 

There is also a `pkgdepends::parse_pkg_refs()` function, which accepts a character vector, so this might just be a typo if the mismatch between documentation and function behaviour isn't intentional.

title: Bioconductor binaries from P3M (`BioC_mirror`) are treated as source packages
description:
When `BioC_mirror` points to Posit Package Manager's Linux binary endpoint, pak downloads prebuilt binaries but treats them as source packages. It then requires build tools, so installation fails on systems without a compiler toolchain, although nothing needs to be compiled.

### Reprex

```r
options(BioC_mirror = "https://packagemanager.posit.co/bioconductor/__linux__/manylinux_2_28/latest")
pak::pak("bioc::DESeq2")
```

```
+ XVector                0.52.0   [bld][cmp][dl]
...
✔ Got XVector 0.52.0 (source) (647.78 kB)
ℹ Building BiocGenerics 0.58.1
Error:
! error in pak subprocess
Caused by error:
! Could not find tools necessary to compile a package
```

### The downloads are binaries

```sh
curl -sL -A 'R (4.6.1 x86_64-pc-linux-gnu x86_64 linux-gnu)' -o XVector.tar.gz \
  https://packagemanager.posit.co/bioconductor/__linux__/manylinux_2_28/latest/packages/3.23/bioc/src/contrib/XVector_0.52.0.tar.gz
tar -tzf XVector.tar.gz | grep '\.so$'
#> XVector/libs/XVector.so
tar -xzOf XVector.tar.gz XVector/DESCRIPTION | grep '^Built:'
#> Built: R 4.6.0; x86_64-pc-linux-gnu; 2026-08-25 05:09:53 UTC; unix
```

With `make` and a compiler on `PATH`, the same call succeeds. Each "build" takes under 2 s and needs no system headers.

### Expected

pak recognizes P3M Bioconductor binary URLs (`/bioconductor/__linux__/<platform>/`) the same way it recognizes `/cran/__linux__/<platform>/`. It installs them as binaries without calling `pkgbuild::check_build_tools()`.

This issue may be related to [this one](https://github.com/r-lib/pkgcache/issues/138)

title: `pak::pak()`/`pkg_install()` fails with 401 Unauthorized on the second of two sequential `git::` remote installs to the same host with different credentials
description:
## Description

When installing two different `git::` remote packages hosted on the **same git host** (same authority/hostname) but authenticated with **different credentials** (`https://TOKEN:<token>@host/path.git` basic-auth-in-URL scheme), the second `pak::pak()` (or `pak::pkg_install()`) call fails with a 401 Unauthorized error — but only when both calls happen **within the same R session/process**. Running the exact same two installs as two separate `Rscript` process invocations works every time.

Claude suggests that  pak/pkgdepends is reusing an HTTP connection, HTTP/2 stream, or some other session-level HTTP client state across `pkg_install()`/`pak()` calls within the same R process, and that reused connection/state is carrying stale Basic-Auth credentials from the first host+token pairing into a second request against the same host with a different token.

The failure happens specifically at pkgdepends' lightweight metadata-fetch step for a `git::` remote (fetching just `DESCRIPTION` to resolve dependencies, not the full clone) — not at the actual git clone step.

## Reprex - sort of...

I could not produce a literal `reprex::reprex()` transcript because reproducing this requires two distinct, independently-authenticated private git repos, which I can't include here (this happened against an internal, self-hosted GitLab instance, and I can't share its hostname, package names, or tokens). Instead, here  **manual reproduction steps** that should work  against **gitlab.com**:

### Setup (one-time, on gitlab.com)

1. Create two throwaway **private** repos on gitlab.com, e.g. `youruser/pkgA` and `youruser/pkgB`. Each just needs a minimal valid `DESCRIPTION` file at its root (a trivial, empty-`R/`-dir package is enough) so pak can resolve it as an R package.
2. On **each** repo, create a separate **Project Access Token** (Settings → Access Tokens), scope `read_repository` only. Call them `TOKEN_A` (for `pkgA`) and `TOKEN_B` (for `pkgB`). Using two *different* tokens is the key part of the reprex — using the same token for both does not seem to trigger this (untested exhaustively, but consistent with our internal reproduction, where the same-token case never failed).
3. Export them in your shell:
   ```bash
   export TOKEN_A="glpat-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx"
   export TOKEN_B="glpat-yyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyyy"
   ```

### Failing case — both installs in one R session

```r
url_a <- paste0("git::https://TOKEN:", Sys.getenv("TOKEN_A"), "@gitlab.com/youruser/pkgA.git")
url_b <- paste0("git::https://TOKEN:", Sys.getenv("TOKEN_B"), "@gitlab.com/youruser/pkgB.git")

pak::pak(url_a)   # succeeds
pak::pak(url_b)   # fails with 401, see error below
```

Run as a single `Rscript -e` call (both lines in the same `-e` string) or sourced from one script — the point is that both `pak::pak()` calls execute in the same R process/pak session.

### Non-failing case — same two installs, separate processes

```bash
Rscript -e 'pak::pak(paste0("git::https://TOKEN:", Sys.getenv("TOKEN_A"), "@gitlab.com/youruser/pkgA.git"))'
Rscript -e 'pak::pak(paste0("git::https://TOKEN:", Sys.getenv("TOKEN_B"), "@gitlab.com/youruser/pkgB.git"))'
```

Both succeed every time when run as two separate `Rscript` invocations.

### What we actually observed against our internal setup (not gitlab.com)

For context, this is the evidence from our own internal reproduction (host/paths/tokens genericized below, matching the shape of the failure exactly):

- Both tokens are valid and correctly scoped (`read_repository`), confirmed independently via `git clone` / `git ls-remote` with each token against its own repo — both succeed every time, in isolation and back-to-back.
- Running `pak::pak(url_b)` **alone**, in its own fresh `Rscript` process (nothing else run first in that R session), always succeeds — reproducible every time tested.
- Running `pak::pak(url_a)` then `pak::pak(url_b)` sequentially in the **same** R process/session — whether via a sourced script, two lines in one `Rscript -e` call, or an automated container-startup script — always fails on the second call with the 401 shown below. This was reproducible every single time tested, including with a fixed 5-second delay and with a retry-with-backoff (4 attempts, growing delays) between the two calls — neither mitigation helped, which rules out a pure timing/rate-limit explanation.
- Only running the two installs as two **separate** `Rscript` process invocations reliably avoided the failure.
- A plain `curl -v` to the git smart-HTTP endpoint of `pkgB`'s repo (`.../info/refs?service=git-upload-pack`), using `pkgB`'s own token, run standalone in the very same environment/container where the automated script fails, succeeds (`HTTP/2 200`) — this rules out network/proxy/firewall/token-validity issues as the cause.
- `pak::pkg_deps()` (dependency resolution only, no install) on `pkgB`'s URL, run standalone, also succeeds and resolves cleanly.

### Actual error

```
Error:
! error in pak subprocess
Caused by error:
! Could not solve package dependencies:
* git::https://PAT:<token2>@host/repo2.git: ! pkgdepends resolution error for
git::https://PAT:<token2>@host/repo2.git.
Caused by error:
! Failed to download 'DESCRIPTION' from git repo at
<https://PAT:<token2>@host/repo2.git>.
Caused by error in `stop(http_error(resp))`:
! Unauthorized (HTTP 401).
```

## Expected vs actual behavior

**Expected:** installing two `git::` remote packages from the same git host but with two different valid, correctly-scoped credentials should succeed regardless of whether the two `pak::pak()`/`pkg_install()` calls happen in the same R session or in separate processes — each install's authentication should be handled independently.

**Actual:** the second install fails with a 401 Unauthorized specifically when both calls happen in the same R session, even though the exact same credential/URL succeeds every time when run in isolation (a fresh process, a standalone `pkg_deps()` call, or a plain `curl` request).

## Environment

- R version: 4.5.x
- pak: latest stable, installed via the official binary channel (`https://r-lib.github.io/p/pak/stable/...`)
- OS: a recent `rocker/r-ver`-based Debian/Ubuntu Docker image
- Network: behind a corporate HTTP/HTTPS forward proxy (`CONNECT`-tunneled to the git host on port 443; TLS 1.3; HTTP/2 negotiated via ALPN on the tunneled connection)
- Git host: a self-hosted GitLab instance (also expected to reproduce against gitlab.com per the reprex above)

**R version:** 4.6.1 (also happens in RStudio Server 2026.05.1 Build 225)
**Operating system:** Ubuntu 24.04.4 running inside an [Apptainer](https://apptainer.org/docs/user/latest/) container on a Rocky 9.6 host
**Environment:** HPC cluster running Slurm and Open OnDemand

**Expected Behavior:**

`pak::pak("<github_user>/<github_repo>")` pulls all required packages and source tarballs to install a package

**Actual Behavior:**

`pak::pak("<github_user>/<github_repo>")` fails on any GitHub zipballs stored at `https://api.github.com/repos/<github_user>/<github_repo>/zipball/<user>`

**Steps to Reproduce the Problem:**

Install `pak` using:

```r
install.packages("pak", repos = sprintf("https://r-lib.github.io/p/pak/stable/%s/%s/%s", .Platform$pkgType, R.Version()$os, R.Version()$arch))
pak::pak_install_extra()
```

Install a package from GitHub using `pak`:

```r
pak::pak("<github_user>/<github_repo>")
```

e.g.

```r
pak::pak("cole-trapnell-lab/monocle3")
```

I'm wondering if this is an "us" issue and if our network access from cluster compute nodes is somehow blocking things, or if we are hitting rate-limiting.

Things I've tried already:

* Using a personal GitHub PAT instead of the one `pak` bundles (WRT warning "`! Using bundled GitHub PAT. Please add your own PAT using gitcreds::gitcreds_set().`") - no change
* `options(pak.download_method = "base")` - didn't work
* `Sys.setenv(CURL_SSL_BACKEND = "openssl")` and `options(pak.client_http_version = "1.1")` - also didn't work

As I say, could be an "us" issue, but any thoughts anyone have most welcome. Since [v.2.5.0 of `devtools` deprecated its install wrappers in favour of `pak`](https://github.com/r-lib/devtools/releases/tag/v2.5.0), this is quite an issue for us (many of our cluster users are heavy `devtools` users for installing from GitHub).

Thanking you in advance!

title: [Feature request] Respect BiocManager's `BIOCONDUCTOR_CONFIG_FILE` setting for Bioconductor config lookup
description:
It is known that Bioconductor mirrors require a configuration file (usually https://bioconductor.org/config.yaml) to work properly. However, I'm working in a environment that has very unstable network access to this default config url.

In BiocManager, I use `BIOCONDUCTOR_CONFIG_FILE` to specify a custom url for the config file. I note that `pak` use the environmental variable `R_BIOC_CONFIG_URL` for the same function. 

It will be nice if pak (pkgcache) can recognize the `BIOCONDUCTOR_CONFIG_FILE` option as well, which will make `pak` easier to configure in environments that already rely on BiocManager.

title: `pak::pkg_install()` does not download manylinux binaries from P3M
description:
### Description

In our multi-stage Docker builds, we require a binary-only installation where packages are exclusively pulled from a `manylinux` URL. 

Standard `install.packages()` works perfectly and downloads the pre-compiled binaries. However, `pak::pkg_install()` treats the repository strictly as a source repository, forcing full local compilations.

`pak::meta_list()[["sources"]]` reveals that `pak` appends `/src/contrib/` to the `manylinux` path instead of parsing it as a binary layout:

```r
[[1]]
[1] "https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/__linux__/manylinux_2_28/2026-06-01/src/contrib/data.table_1.15.4.tar.gz"
```

This classification failure could be a regression/side effect of the broader regular expression changes introduced in **v0.9.5 (#863)**. The internal URL classification patterns (such as `pkgcache:::is_ppm_linux_repo_url()`) do not recognize the `manylinux_2_28` distribution string as a valid PPM binary architecture tag, causing `pak` to fall back to a source mapping strategy.

---

### Steps to Reproduce

```r
options(
  repos = c(
    P3M_MANYLINUX = "https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/__linux__/manylinux_2_28/2026-06-01"
  )
)

# Under the hood, this resolves to /src/contrib/ and triggers a source build:
pak::meta_list("data.table")[["sources"]]

# Fails to pull pre-compiled binary:
pak::pkg_install("data.table")
```

description:
Hello, I am attempting to install pak per the documentation for pre-built binaries (bold added for emphasis):

> Our pre-built binaries have the advantage that they are completely self-contained and dependency free. **No additional R packages, system libraries or tools (e.g. compilers)** are needed for them. Install a pre-built binary build of pak from our repository on GitHub:
> 
> `install.packages("pak", repos = sprintf(
>   "https://r-lib.github.io/p/pak/stable/%s/%s/%s",
>   .Platform$pkgType,
>   R.Version()$os,
>   R.Version()$arch))`

Pak downloads but fails to install. Here are the warnings:

> WARNING: Rtools is required to build R packages but is not currently installed. Please download and install the appropriate version of Rtools before proceeding:
> 
> https://cran.rstudio.com/bin/windows/Rtools/
> 
> Warning: unable to access index for repository https://r-lib.github.io/p/pak/stable/win.binary/mingw32/x86_64/src/contrib:

> A version of this package for your version of R might be available elsewhere,

> https://cran.r-project.org/doc/manuals/r-patched/R-admin.html#Installing-packages

That warning sounds a bit counter-intuitive, or I'm not fully understanding the nature of pre-builts and pak. I do not have Rtools installed. My R version is 4.5.3. Thanks in advance for the help.

title: `Error restoring session`
description:
Everytime I install a new package with {pak} and then I restart my R session, I get this message:

```
Error restoring session (console_actions): An error occurred while parsing json.
```

It’s not a critical error; the package is installed correctly and works fine. But it’s a bit odd to see this message.

Title: [BUG] Build failure installing pak v0.11.0 (Windows/R 4.6/rtools45) - Log truncated
Environment:

OS: Windows (x86_64-w64-mingw32)
R Version: R 4.6.0 (C:/PROGRA~1/R/R-46~1.0)
Toolchain: rtools45 (GCC 14.3.0)
Package: pak version 0.11.0 (installed via renv)
Description:
Attempting to install the pak package from source fails during the compilation of its bundled dependencies. The build process successfully compiles R6, cli, curl, filelock, and jsonlite, but the provided error log cuts off abruptly while compiling the lpSolve dependency, hiding the actual fatal error.

Observed Warnings in Log:
While these may not be the root cause, the build generates a high volume of compiler warnings with the new GCC 14.3.0 toolchain:

lpSolve (C code): Dozens of -Wmaybe-uninitialized, -Wunused-but-set-variable, and -Wmisleading-indentation warnings. (e.g., in hbio.c, lp_MPS.c, lp_presolve.c, sparselib.c).
jsonlite (R code): Missing S4 method definitions for classes like "AsIs", "ITime", "hms", "integer64", and "sf". This is likely benign and just indicates missing suggested packages, but worth noting.
cli (C code): Uninitialized variable warning in diff.c.
Steps to Reproduce:

Open R 4.6.0 on Windows with rtools45 active.
Run renv::restore() (or equivalent command) that triggers a from-source installation of pak 0.11.0.
Observe the build failure.
Expected Behavior:
pak and its bundled dependencies compile cleanly and install successfully.

Actual Behavior:
Installation halts. The log ends exactly here:

````
gcc  -I"C:/PROGRA~1/R/R-46~1.0/include" -DNDEBUG -I . -DINTEGERTIME ... -c sparselib.c -o sparselib.o
sparselib.c: In function 'dswapVector1':
sparselib.c:823:10: warning: variable 'd' set but not used [-Wunused-but-set-variable]
  823 |   int i, d, n;
      |          ^
[...]
Action Required / Next Steps:
````

@Reporter: Please provide the tail end of the build log (the lines immediately following [...] in your text file). The fatal error (e.g., a missing header, a linking error, or an actual compiler error -Werror) is required to diagnose the root cause.
Hypothesis: Given the strictness of GCC 14, it is possible that a downstream compiler flag is treating one of the many lpSolve warnings as a fatal error, or there is a missing library dependency for lpSolve that hasn't been reached yet in the log output.

title: Installing package from GitHub repository containing symlink fails
description:
On trying to install a package `bridgestan` using a `github` package reference with subdirectory specifier using `pak` with

```R
pak::pkg_install("github::roualdes/bridgestan/R@v2.6.2")
```

locally (on Ubuntu 24.04 or within a `posit/r-base:4.5-noble` Docker container, both with `pak@v0.9.0`) or on `macos-latest` / `ubuntu-latest` GitHub Actions runners I get an error

```
<callr_error/rlib_error_3_0/rlib_error/error>
Error:
! error in pak subprocess
Caused by error in `stop_task_package_uncompress(state, worker)`:
! Failed to uncompress bridgestan from /tmp/Rtmp9FJYBP/file2d24eb3b88/src/contrib/bridgestan_2.6.2_2fc2521.tar.gz-t.
---
Backtrace:
1. pak::pkg_install("github::roualdes/bridgestan/R@v2.6.2")
2. pak:::remote(function(...) get("pkg_install_do_plan", asNamespace("pak"))(...), …
3. err$throw(res$error)
---
Subprocess backtrace:
 1. base::withCallingHandlers(cli_message = function(msg) { …
 2. get("pkg_install_do_plan", asNamespace("pak"))(...)
 3. proposal$install()
 4. pkgdepends::install_package_plan(plan, lib = private$library, num_workers = nw, …
 5. base::withCallingHandlers({ …
 6. pkgdepends:::handle_events(state, events)
 7. pkgdepends:::handle_event(state, i)
 8. pkgdepends:::stop_task(state, worker)
 9. pkgdepends:::stop_task_package(state, worker)
10. pkgdepends:::stop_task_package_uncompress(state, worker)
11. base::throw(pkg_error("Failed to uncompress {.pkg {pkg}} from\n      {.path {state$plan$file[[pkgidx]]}}.", …
12. | base::signalCondition(cond)
13. global (function (e) …
```

As far as I can tell the package reference follows the [format specified in the documentation](https://pak.r-lib.org/reference/pak_package_sources.html#github-packages-github-).

Installing via `remotes::install_github` instead using

```R
remotes::install_github("https://github.com/roualdes/bridgestan", subdir="R", ref="v2.6.2")
```

works without issues.

I originally noticed this issue as a series of GitHub Actions workflows using `setup-r-dependencies` with `bridgestan` specified in the `extra-packages` argument started failing on MacOS / Ubuntu due to the above error (UCL/rmcmc#92) - interestingly however the installation proceeds without errors when running on the Windows runners - for example [see the logs from this workflow run](https://github.com/UCL/rmcmc/actions/runs/16734158839).

From a bit of further investigation locally: the downloaded package file `bridgestan_2.6.2_2fc2521.tar.gz-t` appears from the extension as if it should be a gzipped tar file but in practice running

```bash
tar -xvzf bridgestan_2.6.2_2fc2521.tar.gz-t
```

gives an error

```
gzip: stdin has more than one entry--rest ignored
tar: Child returned status 2
tar: Error is not recoverable: exiting now
```

Running 

```bash
file bridgestan_2.6.2_2fc2521.tar.gz-t
```

outputs

```
bridgestan_2.6.2_2fc2521.tar.gz-t: Zip archive data, at least v1.0 to extract, compression method=store
```

suggesting it is instead a zip archive, and this appears to be the case as running

```
unzip bridgestan_2.6.2_2fc2521.tar.gz-t
```

succeeds.

So possibly the issue here is that the automatic identification of the archive type and so correct command to uncompress the archive is failing?

title: Duplicate pre_install system requirements entries and double slash in source URLs in lockfile
description:
# Description
When generating a lockfile using pak (version 0.9.2), I am observing two issues that seem unintended.

## 1. Duplicate entries in pre_install

The generated lockfile contains duplicated commands in the pre_install section. For example:
```
"pre_install": [  "apt-get -y update",  "curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh -s -- --no-modify-path -y",  "curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh -s -- --no-modify-path -y"]Show more lines`
```
The Rust installation command appears twice, identically. *Additional context*: This seems to happen when multiple dependencies require Rust. In my case:

- Previously I had a rust dependent package
- I then installed yaml12, which also requires Rust

My assumption is that each package contributes its own system requirement, and these are not deduplicated when generating the lockfile.

### Expected behavior
System requirement installation steps should be deduplicated so that each command appears only once.

### Observed behavior
Commands are repeated when multiple dependencies declare the same system requirement (e.g. Rust).

## 2. Double slash in source URLs

The sources field in the lockfile sometimes contains URLs with a double slash before src, e.g.:
```
"sources": [  "https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/2026-01-29/bin/linux/noble-x86_64/4.5//src/contrib/backports_1.5.0.tar.gz"]
```

### Additional context
Previously, lockfiles generated from the same (or equivalent) snapshot contained URLs with a single slash:
```
.../4.5/src/contrib/...
```
Now, when rebuilding the lockfile (even using the same snapshot), the URLs contain a double slash:
```
../4.5//src/contrib/...
```

This suggests a change in how URLs are constructed (e.g. concatenation without normalizing trailing/leading slashes).

### Expected behavior

URLs should be normalized to avoid double slashes:

```
.../4.5/src/contrib/...
```

### Observed behavior
A `//` appears due to concatenation of base URLs ending in / and paths starting with /.

### Comments


The duplicate pre_install entries are functionally harmless (Rust installer is idempotent), but:

- make the lockfile noisier
- can slow down builds
- may cause confusion

The double slash in URLs does not seem to break functionality, but:

- introduces unnecessary diffs in version control
- suggests missing normalization

## Environment

pak version: 0.9.2
R version: 4.5
OS: Ubuntu



## Question

Is this the expected behavior, or should:

- system requirement commands be deduplicated across dependencies?
- repository URLs be normalized when constructing source paths?

title: More informative error message when packages are removed from CRAN
description:
If you attempt to upgrade a package that has been removed from CRAN, you get an uninformative error message:

```r
pak::pkg_install("hdi", upgrade = TRUE)
> Error:                                                                      
> ! error in pak subprocess
> Caused by error in `if (candidate$type == "installed" && package_version(resolution$version) > …`:
> ! missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed
```

Of course, if you're attempting to upgrade a specific package like in the above, this is easy to diagnose. But if you're upgrading a bunch of packages, you have no idea which package(s) is causing the issue:

```r
pak::pkg_install(all_my_packages, upgrade = TRUE)
> Error:                                                                      
> ! error in pak subprocess
> Caused by error in `if (candidate$type == "installed" && package_version(resolution$version) > …`:
> ! missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed
```

Leading to a painful process of trying to hunt down the offending package.

title: `pkg_install()` fails on set of packages: `filelock` not found, then `install_extracted_binary` not found
description:
## Summary

With `pak devel 0.10.0.9000`, `R 4.6.0 (manylinux_2_34`) on `ubuntu:24.04`, and PPM's `__linux__/manylinux_2_28` repo configured:

- `pak::pkg_install('data.table')` and
  `pak::pkg_install(c('data.table', 'stringr', 'sf'))` work fine. The same packages install fine with simple `install.packages()`.
- But `pak::pkg_install()` on 80 packages (see list below) fails. The PPM binaries exist for these  packages (confirmed via `meta_list()` and `install.packages()`).

## Reproduction

```r
options(repos = c(P3M_MANYLINUX = "https://packagemanager.posit.co/cran/__linux__/manylinux_2_28/2026-06-01"))

cran_packages <- c(
  'AER', 'AICcmodavg', 'arthistory', 'babynames', 'brms', 'caret', 'clue',
  'crayon', 'data.table', 'devtools', 'downlit', 'ellmer', 'friends',
  'GGally', 'gganimate', 'ggdist', 'gghighlight', 'gifski', 'ggpubr',
  'ggrepel', 'ggridges', 'ggthemes', 'glmmTMB', 'gridExtra', 'gt',
  'janitor', 'knitr', 'languageserver', 'lmerTest', 'mclust',
  'microbenchmark', 'mlr', 'moderndive', 'MuMIn', 'nycflights23',
  'openintro', 'ordinal', 'polycor', 'quanteda', 'quanteda.textmodels',
  'quanteda.textplots', 'quanteda.textstats', 'randomForest', 'Rcpp',
  'RCurl', 'readtext', 'renv', 'reticulate', 'rmarkdown', 'RODBC',
  'rvest', 'sandwich', 'scales', 'sf', 'showtext', 'stm', 'tidygam',
  'tidymodels', 'tidytext', 'tidyverse', 'udpipe', 'xml2',
  'corrplot', 'effects', 'Epi', 'epitools', 'EValue', 'ggeffects',
  'ggfortify', 'gmodels', 'gtsummary', 'Hmisc', 'marginaleffects',
  'mice', 'naniar', 'performance', 'pROC', 'psych', 'ResourceSelection',
  'rms', 'summarytools'
)

pak::pkg_install(cran_packages)
```

## Error 1 (filelock missing)

The call above fails with:

```
! in callr subprocess.
Caused by error in `loadNamespace(x)`:
! there is no package called 'filelock'
---
Subprocess backtrace:
1. options$post_process()
2. pkgdepends:::install_extracted_binary(filename, lib_cache, pkg_cache, lib, ...
3. pkgdepends:::lock_cache(lib_cache, pkg_name, getOption("install.lock"))
4. base::loadNamespace(x)
```

This looks like a recurrence of #197, where `filelock` was likewise reported missing. 

## Error 2 (after installing filelock)

```r
install.packages('filelock', repos = 'https://cloud.r-project.org')
pak::pkg_install(cran_packages)  # same list as above
```

New internal error:

```
! in callr subprocess.
Caused by error in `install_extracted_binary(filename, lib_cache, pkg_cache, lib, ...`:
! could not find function "install_extracted_binary"
```

JJ

title: (Speculative) `get_locked_libs()` is not safe for vector-valued `lib` on Windows
description:
Me still poking around this new feature 😄. This is an incidental observation made by Posit AI while working on something else, but it seems plausible. Sorry I don't have a warm Windows machine at the moment to repro. Below is basically copy/paste LLM analysis but it has the ring of truth. And if I start doing this in devtools and Positron, we're going to find out!

---

`get_locked_libs()` in `R/warn-loaded.R` is called on Windows to check whether any DLLs belonging to packages-to-be-installed are currently locked by an R process. It receives a `lib` argument that now can be a character vector.

The bug is in this line:

https://github.com/r-lib/pak/blob/c57be1b62152cc7c2b600efceeb56b31ad194cc6/R/warn-loaded.R#L278

`file.path()` recycles its arguments element-wise, so when both `lib` and `pkgs` are vectors, the result is not the full cross-product of libraries × packages. Instead it silently interleaves them:

```
file.path(c("/libA", "/libB"), c("foo", "bar", "baz"), "libs")
# [1] "/libA/foo/libs"  "/libB/bar/libs"  "/libA/baz/libs"
```

`foo` is only checked in `libA`, `bar` only in `libB`, `baz` only in `libA` — regardless of which library each package actually lives in. This means locked DLLs can be silently missed.

This only manifests when a caller passes a vector to `lib`, which is newly supported by `pkg_install()` and the `local_install_*` family but not yet documented. It is not currently reachable in normal pak usage since the default is `.libPaths()[1]`.

title: Internal subprocess does not inherit R session options
description:
Hi,

Recently, when using the package, I've discovered a bug (unless it's a feature :)) when using `pak::pkg_sysreqs`. However, I suspect that it might extend to other functions using subprocesses. In a nutshell, it looks like subprocesses do not inherit the R session options from their parent process. I discovered it while developing the package that has a user .RProfile. Among many lines there is one that says: `options(download.file.method = "wininet", timeout = 300)` which is part of our enterprise process for Linux. I started the session with --vanilla flag, wanting to ignore the .RProfile for the time being; however, when called `pak::pkg_sysreqs`, it led to errors as it uses the Windows option from .RProfile. I believe that the unexpected result comes from the fact that although the main process is run without .RProfile, with --vanilla mode, the subporcess which resolves requirements is run with standard options and hence reads the startup configuration. In my opinion, it is a bit of an unexpected result as if someone runs their session in the --vanilla mode, they probably expect that to be carried forward to subprocesses. Alternatively, an option to configure it using system variables would be really appreciated.

title: Finishing touches re: considering installed packages in multiple libraries
description:
I'm very excited to take advantage of this change in `devtools::install()` and, then, in the "install this package" gesture in Positron:

https://github.com/r-lib/pkgdepends/commit/634661a7d91b41476fd1ab653fe3087a6e40b8a9

This *should* be ready to go as of pak 0.9.3, however, I think I've found 2 loose ends that have to get fixed first, one in pkgdepends and another in pak itself. I'll make a pure pak PR, just to show what I mean (I realize pak embeds pkgdepends).

---

pak 0.9.3 added support for passing a character vector to `lib` in `local_install_deps()`, so that pak can consult multiple libraries when deciding what needs to be installed (while still installing new packages only to `lib[1]`).

*Side note: the docs for `lib` don't seem to reflect this change and I'm honestly a bit foggy on which functions this new feature applies to, beyond `local_install_deps()`.*

However, I think two code paths still need an update to handle a vector `lib`.

Imagine I'm working on rematch2 locally and I execute `devtools::install()`, which now uses `pak::local_install_deps()` for dependencies:

https://github.com/r-lib/devtools/blob/a3447b9f3d59abb6cc8b63a54db3435819324c1e/R/install.R#L78-L103

Imagine I've got some library in front of the main library(ies) where add-on packages live.

### CRAN releases of devtools and pak

I've installed devtools and pak like so:

```r
pak::pak(c("devtools", "pak"))
```

Problem: rematch2 **and its entire dependency tree** get installed into `.libPaths()[[1]]`, even though I already have all those dependencies installed at suitable versions in later lib paths.

``` r
usethis::local_project("~/work/rematch2")
#> ✔ Setting active project to "/Users/jenny/work/rematch2".
packageVersion("devtools")
#> [1] '2.5.1'
packageVersion("pak")
#> [1] '0.9.4'

tmp_lib <- fs::dir_create(fs::path_temp("tmp_lib"))
withr::local_libpaths(tmp_lib, action = "prefix")

devtools::install()
#> ── pak::local_install_deps() ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> ℹ Loading metadata database
#> ✔ Loading metadata database ... done
#> 
#> 
#> → Will install 10 packages.
#> ...
#> * DONE (rematch2)

.libPaths()
#> [1] "/private/tmp/Rtmpa3v4yN/tmp_lib"                                     
#> [2] "/Users/jenny/Library/R/arm64/4.5/library"                            
#> [3] "/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/4.5-arm64/Resources/library"

fs::path_file(fs::dir_ls(tmp_lib))
#>  [1] "_cache"    "cli"       "glue"      "lifecycle" "magrittr"  "pillar"   
#>  [7] "pkgconfig" "rematch2"  "rlang"     "tibble"    "utf8"      "vctrs"

pak::pkg_status(c("cli", "glue")) |>
  dplyr::select(package, library, version) |>
  dplyr::arrange(package)
#> # A data frame: 4 × 3
#>   package library                                  version
#>   <chr>   <chr>                                    <chr>  
#> 1 cli     /private/tmp/Rtmpa3v4yN/tmp_lib          3.6.6  
#> 2 cli     /Users/jenny/Library/R/arm64/4.5/library 3.6.6  
#> 3 glue    /private/tmp/Rtmpa3v4yN/tmp_lib          1.8.1

```

Packages like cli and glue are already present in my user library.
This re-installation can be very time consuming, which has been noted by devtools and Positron users after the pivot towards pak (mostly linux folks, I believe?).

### devtools PR and CRAN release of pak

I've installed devtools and pak like so:

```r
pak::pak("pak")
pak::pak("r-lib/devtools#2690")
```

Problem: there's an error originating in pkgdepends logic and a warning coming from pak.
Nothing gets installed.

title: pak does not see system dependencies under non default path

title: pak cannot download from repos with self-issued certificates
description:
this works:

```r
pak::pkg_install("git::https://github.com/tidyverse/ggplot2.git")
```

this fails:

```r
pak::pkg_install("git::https://hooli.local/foo/bar.git") # website with self-issued certificate
```

with
```
Error:                                                                                                          
! error in pak subprocess
Caused by error: 
! Could not solve package dependencies:
* git::https://hooli.local/foo/bar.git: ! pkgdepends resolution error for git::https://hooli.local/foo/bar.git.
Caused by error: 
! Failed to download DESCRIPTION from git repo at <https://hooli.local/foo/bar.git>.
Caused by error in `(function (e) …`:
! SSL certificate problem: unable to get local issuer certificate
Type .Last.error to see the more details.
```

this works:

```sh
curl https://hooli.local/foo/bar
```

this works:

```r
remotes::install_git("https://hooli.local/foo/bar.git)"
```

I have placed the self-issued certificate into `/etc/ssl/certs` and then run `sudo update-ca-certificates`.

I've also set `options(async_http_cainfo = "/etc/ssl/certs")` in my `.Rprofile` to override the certificates that pak ships with.

This is hard to debug, because I don't have ready access to a share-able website with a self-issued certificate, and I know this is usually/probably a user issue.

It's odd however, that `curl` otherwise works, but pak doesn't, even `options(async_http_cainfo = "/etc/ssl/certs")`.
Is there any other way in which pak and `curl` calls still differ when this option is set?

title: r-lib/actions/setup-r-dependencies@v2 fails on github enterprise cloud since pak v.0.9.3 when using internal package installation via Remotes
description:
Since the update to v.0.9.3 I can't install internal packages via the Remotes field in the DESCRIPTION using the github action setup-r-dependencies which uses pak.

The AI agent gave me this as the likely reason:

The error originates from pak 0.9.3 (released April 8-9, 2026, bundling pkgdepends 0.9.1). When pak resolves dependencies, it reads the Remotes field from DESCRIPTION files and passes entries like packagename=git :: https://enterprise.ghe.com/ORG/packagename.git to
parse_pkg_refs() -> get_remote_types(). In the new version, this parsing fails with "Cannot parse package".

The critical flow (dep-utils.R:89-95):

# resolve_ref_deps() always parses ALL Remotes entries eagerly:
if (!is.na(remotes)) {
remotes <- str_trim(na.omit(remotes))
remotes <- parse(remotes)
remotes packages <- check_names(parse_pkg_refs(remotes)) # <-- fails HERE
...



The commit history between 0.9.0 and 0.9.1 includes a bulk "reformat with air" (85fac3e), which is the most likely source of a subtle regex/parsing regression in how pkg-git :: url is handled.

Cheers

title: Rust bootstrap silently fails on fresh Ubuntu 22.04 when curl is missing
description:
`pak` silently fails to bootstrap Rust on fresh Ubuntu 22.04 when `curl` is missing

I can reproduce this in a fresh `rocker/r2u:jammy` container.

Minimal failing repro:

```bash
docker run --rm --platform linux/amd64 rocker/r2u:jammy \
  bash -lc 'apt-get update >/dev/null && apt-get install -y r-cran-pak >/dev/null && R -q -e '\''pak::pak("hellorust")'\'''
```

This logs:

```text
ℹ Executing `sh -c curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh -s -- --no-modify-path -y`
```

and then later fails because `cargo` / `rustc` are still not found.

I can reproduce the same behavior with a `rextendr` package as well:

```bash
docker run --rm --platform linux/amd64 rocker/r2u:jammy \
  bash -lc 'apt-get update >/dev/null && apt-get install -y r-cran-pak >/dev/null && R -q -e '\''pak::pak("tergo")'\'''
```

In this base image, `curl` is not installed:

```bash
docker run --rm --platform linux/amd64 rocker/r2u:jammy \
  bash -lc 'which curl || true'
```

If I preinstall `curl`, the same `pak` install succeeds for `hellorust`:

```bash
docker run --rm --platform linux/amd64 rocker/r2u:jammy \
  bash -lc 'apt-get update >/dev/null && apt-get install -y curl r-cran-pak >/dev/null && R -q -e '\''pak::pak("hellorust")'\'''
```

So this looks like the Rust bootstrap command is being run via a shell pipeline where `curl: not found` is masked, and `pak` proceeds as if the bootstrap succeeded.

Expected behavior:
- fail the Rust bootstrap step if `curl` is missing, or
- ensure `curl` is installed before using that command, or
- avoid the shell pipeline in a way that preserves the real exit status

Related reports:
- https://github.com/hadley/bananarama/issues/2
- https://github.com/posit-dev/r-yaml12/issues/8

title: `use_bioconductor = FALSE` still contacts bioconductor.org
description:
Related issue for previous versions of R : https://github.com/r-lib/pak/issues/295


When setting options(pkg.use_bioconductor = FALSE) to avoid Bioconductor entirely (e.g. in a corporate environment where bioconductor.org is blocked), pak still makes an HTTP request to https://bioconductor.org/config.yaml and fails.

To reproduce: Use R 4.5+ behind a firewall with bioconductor.org blocked, set options(pkg.use_bioconductor = FALSE), then call any meta_*() or repo_*() function.

Root cause: In cmc__get_repos(), bioconductor$get_repos() is called unconditionally — before the if (bioc) guard — to classify user-configured repos as type "bioc" vs "cranlike". On R <= 4.4, this is harmless because the builtin R→Bioc version map short-circuits before any network call. On R 4.5+, R 4.5 is intentionally absent from that builtin map, so it falls through to a live HTTP fetch of the Bioconductor config YAML.

Fix : 
```R
# R/metadata-cache.R, inside cmc__get_repos()

# before
bioc_names <- bioconductor$get_repos()

# after
bioc_names <- if (bioc) bioconductor$get_repos() else character(0L)
```

title: `pak` unable to install Linux binary packages from PPM's new `bin/linux` repo URLs
description:
This was first reported by @markrtucker

PPM just added support for Linux binary repo URLs like https://p3m.dev/cran/latest/bin/linux/noble-x86_64/4.5, which are equivalent to the existing `__linux__/noble` URLs but instead encode the R version and arch in the URL and not the user agent. Same as R-universe's Linux binary URLs.

These URLs don't seem to be working with pak though for some reason, as pak seemingly downloads the binary but ends up compiling a source package instead.

Here's a repro for Ubuntu 24 using Boom as an example:

```r
options(repos = c(CRAN = sprintf("https://p3m.dev/cran/latest/bin/linux/noble-%s/%s", R.version["arch"], substr(getRversion(), 1, 3))))

pak::pkg_install("Boom")

# ℹ Getting 1 pkg (2.50 MB)
# ✔ Got Boom 0.9.16 (source) (118.46 MB)                              
# ✔ Downloaded 1 package (118.46 MB) in 4.5s                          
# ℹ Building Boom 0.9.16
# ✔ Built Boom 0.9.16 (1m 45.3s)                             
```

pak gets the Boom binary, the 118 MB file, but still compiles a source package for some reason. The 2.50 MB file above matches the Boom source file.

pak can install from R-universe Linux binary repo URLs just fine though. I am not sure what the difference is, but I did see that R-universe PACKAGES files have a `Platform` field in them. I haven't heard about the Platform field anywhere though, except seeing it in this recent issue https://github.com/r-lib/pak/issues/773

title: Feature Request: Allow passing a multi-line string of packages to pak::pak()
description:
Hi @gaborcsardi  

I was thinking it would be super handy if `pak::pak()` could also accept a plain multi-line string (in addition to a character vector with lots of quotes and commas). It makes copy-pasting and managing large lists of dependencies much easier.

Ideally, the function would ignore blank lines, trim spaces, and let us use `#` to comment out specific packages.

Here's a quick helper function I wrote to show what I mean:

```r
parse_packages <- function(text) {
  pkgs <- unlist(strsplit(text, "\n"))
  pkgs <- trimws(pkgs)
  pkgs <- pkgs[!grepl("^#", pkgs)]
  pkgs <- pkgs[pkgs != ""]
  return(pkgs)
}
```

Usage:
```r
pak::pak(parse_packages("
# ...........................................
# Requirements 
# ...........................................
  dplyr
  lme4
  # ggplot2
  tidyverse/tibble
  
"))
```

Would it make sense to support this natively in `pak()`, or include a small helper function like this to do the heavy lifting?

title: `upgrade=FALSE` ignores system-wide installed packages
description:
Hello,

Since `devtools::install_dev_deps` is going to be deprecated in favor of `pak::local_install_dev_deps` I tried it and stumbled upon the problem that `pak` ignores any already system-wide installed packages (in my case installed by r2u in a docker environment). I understand from the documentation it's partially by design and follows from `lib = .libPaths()[1]` in the arguments. 

Is it really by design? It's very confusing to me at the moment. Is there a way to account for all the packages and install only the packages that are really absent? 

Thanks,
Alexy

title: Package versions not respected?
description: The main point for me of using `pak` is that I can be sure that specified versions are respected: I manage production deployments where I need to strictly maintain dependency chains and ensure things are as they should be. But I recently saw this part of the `pak` docs: which seems to negate the whole point of having the version specifier. I've seen this in practice, where I request a specific version of a package and a different version gets installed (here `myPkg` is a stand-in name for a local package from our local repository, but all the rest of the text is unmodified): ``` > pak::pkg_install("myPkg@2.104.3022540") <------- 2.104.3022540 requested ✔ Loading metadata database ... done → Will install 1 package. → The package (0 B) is cached. + myPkg 2.114-5739970 👷🏻‍♂️ ℹ No downloads are needed, 1 pkg is cached ✔ Installed myPkg 2.114-5739970 (21ms) <------- 2.114-5739970 installed ✔ 1 pkg + 106 deps: kept 103, added 1 [6.2s] ``` Is there a summary of what situations will respect a version constraint, and what situations won't? I'd like to understand this better.

title: Don't execute `can_sudo_without_pw()` until/unless it's absolutely necessary
description:
The next release of devtools uses `pak::local_install_deps()` for installing dependencies inside `devtools::install()`. I learned the hard way, i.e. via unsuccessful CRAN submission, that this can actually lead to a call to `sudo`.

I've now taken measures to ensure that devtools doesn't inadvertently trigger this, now or in the future. But it would also be nice if pak didn't call `sudo -s id` until/unless it has a proven need to know this information.

#> ! error in pak subprocess
#> Caused by error in `process_initialize(...)`:
#> ! Native call to `processx_exec` failed
#> Caused by error:
#> ! create process 'C:/Users/.../pak/library/zip/bin/x64/cmdunzip.exe'
#>   (system error 1260, This program is blocked by group policy.)
```

The root cause is that `pkgdepends:::make_install_process()` calls `make_unzip_process()` → `zip::unzip_process()`, which spawns `cmdunzip.exe` as an external process. Corporate group policy blocks this `.exe`.

Standard R configuration (`R_UNZIPCMD`, `options(unzip=)`, `TAR`) has no effect (I had TAR available on my corporate PC) because pak's internal code path ignores all of these.

## Impact

This completely blocks pak on corporate Windows. The alternative is `install.packages()`, which loses pak's parallel downloads and dependency resolution and takes 6-10x longer (over an hour vs ~10 minutes in my case).

## Proposed solution

**Short term:** Add a pak configuration option (e.g., `PKG_ZIP_METHOD = "internal"`) that tells `pkgdepends` to use `zip::unzip()` (in-process C code, no external `.exe`) instead of `zip::unzip_process()` for `.zip` extraction.

**Long term:** The upstream fix belongs in the `zip` package — see [r-lib/zip#135.](https://github.com/r-lib/zip/issues/135) If `zip::unzip_process()` could fall back to `zip::unzip()` when process creation fails, pak would inherit the fix automatically.

## Working workaround

We developed a patch that replaces `make_install_process` in pak's worker subprocess. It extracts `.zip` files synchronously using `zip::unzip()`, then returns a real `processx::process` object (a finished `cmd /c exit 0`) so pak's async polling loop continues normally. Non-zip archives use the original code path.

```r
library(pak)

pak:::remote(function() {
  ns <- asNamespace("pkgdepends")
  original <- get("make_install_process", envir = ns)

  replacement <- function(filename, lib = .libPaths()[[1L]], metadata = NULL) {
    type <- ns$detect_package_archive_type(filename)
    if (type != "zip") return(original(filename, lib = lib, metadata = metadata))

    now <- Sys.time()
    lib_cache <- ns$library_cache(lib)
    ns$mkdirp(pkg_cache <- tempfile(tmpdir = lib_cache))
    zip::unzip(filename, exdir = pkg_cache, overwrite = TRUE)
    ns$install_extracted_binary(filename, lib_cache, pkg_cache, lib, metadata, now)

    p <- processx::process$new("cmd.exe", c("/c", "exit", "0"),
                                stdout = "|", stderr = "2>&1")
    p$wait()
    reg.finalizer(p, function(...) unlink(pkg_cache, recursive = TRUE), onexit = TRUE)
    p
  }

  unlockBinding("make_install_process", ns)
  assign("make_install_process", replacement, envir = ns)
  lockBinding("make_install_process", ns)
  invisible(TRUE)
})

pak::pkg_install("dplyr")  # works
```

Tested successfully with 100+ packages on Windows 11 Enterprise with AppLocker.
Only issue with this is I have to `source("patch_pak.R")` after each `library(pak)` load or jam it into my `.Rprofile`, which would be fine if it was just me, but there's a few hundred R users where I am.

## Environment

- Windows 11 Enterprise with AppLocker/SRP enabled
- R 4.4.x
- pak 0.8.0+

title: Add support for installing packages from authenticated repositories, with `keyring` support
description:
We're expecting to add an authenticated repositories feature to Posit Package Manager soon. Because we're hoping to support both Python and R, we're limited by the fact that `pip` and friends only support HTTP Basic Auth. So we know there won't be e.g. complex OAuth flows involved.

Now, it's technically possible to install packages from repos that use basic authentication today, e.g. with

```r
options(repos = c(CRAN = "https://username:password@ppm.internal/cran/latest"))
```

but I'm really not a fan of this approach because I think it will lead users to copy around and embed plaintext credentials in configuration files. We've also found that it can cause issues on Windows if the password is too long -- which it will be in the case of a JWT.

Instead, I think we should [follow the example of tools like `pip` and `uv` here](https://pip.pypa.io/en/stable/topics/authentication/#keyring-support), too, by checking the system keyring for passwords automatically.

(`renv` also has a [very flexible mechanism for configuring auth headers](https://rstudio.github.io/renv/articles/package-install.html#custom-headers) that could be wired up to the system keyring, too.)

For example, when `pak` is installing packages from a repository URL like `https://username@ppm.internal/cran/latest`, we could automatically check whether there is a corresponding "password" (or more likely, a token or API key or some kind) in the system keyring and use that to construct an `Authorization` header:

```r
repo_auth <- function(repo_url) {
  if (!is_installed("keyring")) {
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  # Pull the username out of the repo URL.
  parsed <- httr2::url_parse(repo_url)
  username <- parsed$username
  if (is.null(username)) {
    return(NULL)
  }

  # Reconsitute the repo URL without the username.
  parsed$username <- NULL
  base_url <- httr2::url_build(parsed)

  tryCatch(
    {
      pwd <- keyring::key_get(base_url, username)
      auth <- paste(username, pwd, sep = ":")
      c("Authorization" = paste("Basic", openssl::base64_encode(auth)))
    },
    error = function(e) NULL
  )
}
```

the above should work with `renv`, too, via `options(renv.download.headers = repo_auth)`.

To help users out, we could also have a utility function to *set* this "password". I'm imagining an API something like the following:

```r
pak::repo_set_auth("https://username@ppm.internal/cran/latest")
```

This would call the equivalent of

```r
keyring::key_set(
  "https://ppm.internal/cran/latest",
  "username",
  prompt = "Password, Token, or API Key: "
)
```

under the hood.

A more advanced implementation might also prompt the user for credentials when a repo returns a `HTTP 401` in an interactive session, and offer to save them in the system keyring. (This is impossible with `install.packages()` because that function swallows `401` responses.)

Note: one could test basic auth support in `pak` by running a local NGINX with basic auth enabled proxying to `https://p3m.dev`.

I'm happy to help out with this, but I need some pointers on where the relevant changes would need to be made.

title: Use renv cache if available
description: I'm not entirely sure what this involves, but if you use pak inside a renv-using project, it would be nice if the packages were installed into the renv global cache, and then symlinked using the using renv system. (So that `pak::pak()` would be equivalent to `install.packages()` inside renv projects.)

title: pak install error in Docker ARM64 architecture running under emulation on AMD64 machine
description:
I'm running into a bit of a niche issue. I have a machine running Windows 11 on AMD64 architecture. I am attempting to build Docker images for ARM64 architectures for which Docker uses QEMU for emulation during the build process. However, when trying to install packages via pak during the build process, pak fails with the following error message:
> Error in remote(function(...) get("pkg_install_make_plan", asNamespace("pak"))(...),  :
  Subprocess is busy or cannot start

To replicate this on Windows, do the following:
- From the console (e.g. Command Prompt) run an R-based ARM64 image under emulation:
`docker run -it --rm --platform linux/arm64 posit/r-base:4.5.2-noble`
- Next, install pak binary per the usual:
    ```
    install.packages("pak", repos = sprintf("https://r-lib.github.io/p/pak/stable/%s/%s/%s", .Platform$pkgType, R.Version()$os, R.Version()$arch))
    ```
- Then attempt to install any package with pak:
    ```
    > pak::pkg_install("renv")
    Error in remote(function(...) get("pkg_install_make_plan", asNamespace("pak"))(...),  :
      Subprocess is busy or cannot start
    ```

I have a gut feeling that this is related to running R/pak under emulation because I've experienced some weird behavior in the past as a result of emulation. However, I want to confirm whether or not this is the case; any help would be appreciated!

title: Pak in Github CI always tries to install from source
description: Hi all, I have recently faced a problem when using the action `r-lib/actions/setup-r-dependencies@v2`. I believe the problem is cause by `pak` trying to install all the dependencies of my package from source. This results in random `x Failed to download XXXX` messages. These message affect different libraries in different runs and not always happen. I have tried many different configurations of my workflow: different runners, removing renv activation (I have it in my project just for local development), setting up `upgrade: (FALSE)` manually. I have removed all the dependencies of my project too to see if this made any difference. The result is that sometimes all the dependencies are downloaded correctly, and others not like in the previous screenshot, but always from source and not from the binaries. The following screenshot is the info that appears in the `Install/Update packages` step with empty Imports/Suggests: I have reviewed the [lockfile.json](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/22536321/lockfile.json) that is generated in the workflow and I can see that all the dependencies have a property `binary: false` so I am assuming this is why pak tries to download sources instead of binaries. However, I cannot think of a reason why ALL of them are marked as `binary: false`. Something to note is that I am running this workflow in a private repository within my organization, I don't know if this makes any difference at all. I have another project that is running the exact same workflow in a public repository and things work just fine there. Any ideas or suggestions that I could try? Thank you very much in advance!

title: Uninformative error from `pkg_install` when installing packages no longer available on requested repository (e.g., CRAN)
description:
I have a script where I update all of my installed packages using the magic of `pak::pkg_list()`, some other things to convert this to a vector of package names (not relevant), and then `pak::pkg_install()`. There are hundreds, and I don't hand-check the vector. I had a longer issue to file a possible bug, but I discovered by checking against `tools::CRAN_package_db()` that it was simply that the package once existed on CRAN, I installed it, and then CRAN removed the package before I tried to update all of my packages. 

This issue is about the error message that is produced, which is uninformative.

MWE:
```r
c("extrafont", "Rttf2pt1") |> pak::pkg_install()
```
This produced:
```r
Error: 
! error in pak subprocess
Caused by error in `if (candidate$type == "installed" && package_version(resolution$version) > …`:

---
Backtrace:

2. pak:::remote(function(...) get("pkg_install_make_plan", asNamespace("pak"))(...), …
3. err$throw(res$error)
---
Subprocess backtrace:
 1. base::withCallingHandlers(cli_message = function(msg) { …
 2. get("pkg_install_make_plan", asNamespace("pak"))(...)
 3. prop$solve()
 4. private$plan$solve(policy = private$policy)
 5. pkgdepends:::pkgplan_solve(self, private, match.arg(policy))
 6. private$create_lp_problem(pkgs, policy)
 7. pkgdepends:::pkgplan__create_lp_problem(self, private, pkgs, policy)
 8. pkgdepends:::pkgplan_i_create_lp_problem(pkgs, private$config, policy)
 9. pkgdepends:::pkgplan_i_lp_dependencies(lp, config)
10. base::lapply(setdiff(seq_len(num_candidates), ruled_out), depconds)
11. local FUN(X[[i]], ...)
12. base::Filter(x = cand, function(c) { …
13. base::unlist(lapply(x, f))
14. base::lapply(x, f)
15. local FUN(X[[i]], ...)
16. base::isTRUE(satisfies_remote(res, pkgs[c, ]))

18. local sat(resolution, candidate, config, ...)
19. base::.handleSimpleError(function (e) …
20. global h(simpleError(msg, call))

A couple of ideas: 
1. Check that packages are available in the requested repository (e.g., CRAN) before building an installation plan. 
2. Either A) produce a warning that some of the requested packages (list packages) are not available on the repository requested and then skip them, or B) an error stating explicitly which packages are not on the repository requested. B) seems safer.

title: Consider changing default number of cores used
description:
Dear `pak` developers. Thank you for this cool project!

I just want to bring up a little pet peeve I often find with how software handles multi-core utilization. 

Spending a lot of time in shared environments makes me a bit wary of tools where utilizing all cores on the machine is the opt-out behavior. I can't even count the number of times that caused issues for either me or my colleagues.

One might argue that defining some global `Ncpus` value is a good practice in such environment in the first place. But in R I almost never encountered a need to use it (most packages treat parallelization as opt-in) and it's still a rake that many people might step on, especially since this behavior is explained as far as I can tell only on the website and [just a bit deeper](https://pak.r-lib.org/reference/pak-config.html) than the first time user would want to dig.

Would you consider changing the default behavior to NOT run in parallel unless `Ncpus` is explicitly set?

title: Blueskies Feature Request: Package features syntax
description:
Just to set the tone, this really isn't a feature request but more of a proposal for something that I think could really benefit the R ecosystem. Since `pak`/`pkgdepends` has its own internals for resolving package dependencies, its probably the only actionable testing grounds for something like this.

### Motivation

I like packages with small dependency footprints, but I also don't like splitting up packages into fragmented packages that have to be kept in-sync for the sake of separating dependencies.

I've been impressed with how `rust` crates have _features_, which are categories of functionality that each have their own sets of additional dependencies and can be turned on or off at install time, bringing a minimal set of dependencies.

With the rise of using `Config/Needs` to start classifying `Suggests` dependencies, I was wondering if this mechanism could be extended to categorize dependencies for _features_.

### Use cases

Frequently I'll find packages that do what I want, but then tack on a feature or two that pulls in a huge set of dependencies. Frequently these are packages that ship a shiny app or optionally integrate with the tidyverse or another data procesing ecosystem. In the stats world, it's not uncommon to integrate with a few different packages that implement similar models.

In all these cases, Suggests dependencies are managed on an ad-hoc basis in each package. 

### Proposal

Some way of flagging a `Config/` category as a feature

(completely impulsive example syntax, primarily for illustrating ideas)

```dcf
Package: pkgfeatdep
Suggests:
    shiny,
    pkgdown
Config/Feature/app:
    Description: interactive app for my package
    Imports:
        shiny
Config/Needs/website:
    pkgdown
```

This can stand on it's own, but to make it useful it would be helpful to hook into how packages are installed so that features can be included when we depend on packages:

```dcf
Package: pkgrevdep
Imports:
    featdep
Config/Needs/Features:
    featdep (app)
```

```r
pak::pak("pkgrevdep")
#> implicitly installs featdep, including feature dependency shiny,
#> but not suggested dependency pkgdown.
```

My hope would be that this would let the R ecosystem migrate toward more mindful use of Suggests packages and provide an ecosystem for handling the installation of necessary Suggests packages without bringing along all of the developer-facing dependencies for testing/formatting/vignette rendering/websites, etc.

title: Consider option `upgrade=NA` instead of hard true or false?
description:
Currently `upgrade=FALSE` in `pkg_install` prefers binary over source, while `TRUE` will always install the latest one.

Packages like `RcppEigen`, `fftw`, `igraph` are kind of hard to compile from source, which makes most packages fail to install if set to `upgrade=TRUE`, especially on many administrated system, where you can't install missing compilers/user don't know how to configure.

I wonder if we can have `upgrade=NA`, where always upgrade the packages, but prefer binary over source?

title: sudo alerts make sysadmins nervous ...
description:
Hello, as a sysadmin I daily get plenty of "sudo" emails from users trying 
```
COMMAND=/bin/bash -c id
```
We found out it is part of "pak" (sysreqs.R) ...

Why do you not just use "sudo -l" to check if the user is allowed to run sudo, which does not send a system alert ?

See "man sudo"
```
-l, --list
             If no command is specified, list the privileges for the invoking user (or the user specified by the -U option) on
             the current host.  A longer list format is used if this option is specified multiple times and the security policy
             supports a verbose output format.

             If a command is specified and is permitted by the security policy, the fully-qualified path to the command is dis‐
             played along with any args. If a command is specified but not allowed by the policy, sudo will exit with a status
             value of 1.
```
Thanks for fixing ...
from a research environment where the users should have more freedom to use use software.
Best without annoying the sysamdin.

title: Warn or Error on Collision?
description:
Related to #800 , when adding R-Forge (or any repo) using

```r
pak::repo_add(RForge = "http://R-Forge.R-project.org")
```

Then there's a collision between the [`patchwork` library on CRAN ](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/patchwork/index.html) and the [`patchwork` library on R-Forge](https://patchwork.r-forge.r-project.org/) -- which are two very different packages. 

I suppose it's not possible to have both packages installed and loaded simultaneously?

But for the purposes of `pak`, perhaps it could do some kind of check of whether the two packages are different or the same? A superficial check would be for the author list...

title: v0.9.0.9000 trying to install private git remote saturates CPU
description:
Perhaps I'm just catching the repo at a bad time, but because of the severity here I wanted to file this just in case it's not already on your radar. 

Since the last release, recovery from a subprocess failing (specifically due to HTTP error when trying to read file tree from git remote) seems to be broken and now continues to spawn new processes until R is unable to allocate new sub processes, leaving all attempts running at 100% cpu usage in the background.

This breaks the R session - at least anything that attempts to spawn a new process like installing a package (with or without `pak`). 

```sh
rm ~/.git-credentials
echo 'url=https://acme.org' | git credential reject
R -e 'pak::cache_delete()'
```

### `v0.9.0`

Expected, subprocess fails and terminates, showing HTTP error suggesting there's a credentials issue

```r
pak::pak("git::https://acme.org/team/pkg.git")
```
```
Error:

Caused by error: 
! Could not solve package dependencies:
*git::https://acme.org/team/pkg.git: ! pkgdepends resolution error for git::https://acme.org/team/pkg.git.
Caused by error: 
! Failed to download DESCRIPTION from git repo at
<https://acme.org/team/pkg.git>.

title: Feature request: use `pkgbuild` to build the package
description:
Related to https://github.com/r-lib/pkgbuild/issues/59

pkgbuild provides a mechanism to avoid copying large files during the build process by using symlinks or similar strategies.

However, when using `pak::pak(".")`, it appears that the entire package directory is copied, which makes the process significantly slower for packages containing large files. In contrast, building the package first with `pkgbuild::build()` and then installing the tarball using `pak::pak("local::../my_pkg.tar.gz")` is much faster:

```r
pkgbuild::build()
pak::pak("local::../rsahmi_0.0.2.9000.tar.gz")
```

title: Error installing packages from certain repos: `package must be a character vector without NAs`
description:
This may be more of a pkgdepends issue, but maybe also some of pak. We hit this error installing via pak first:
```r
# * curl: ! pkgdepends resolution error for curl.
# Caused by error: 
# ! package must be a character vector without NAs
# Type .Last.error to see the more details.
```

I don't know what exactly reproduces this error, but we're seeing it in various repo setups that have custom packages added to them. For example, here's a setup with a CRAN repo and another repo `local` with custom packages - there are just a handful of old CRAN packages in there. When installing any package from these two repos, pak fails, but `install.packages()` works fine.
```r
options(repos = c(
    CRAN = "https://cloud.r-project.org",
    local = "https://solo.packagemanager.posit.co/local/latest"
))

pak::pkg_install("curl")
# ✔ Updated metadata database: 3.17 MB in 8 files.                          
# ✖ Updating metadata database ... failed                                   
# Error:                                                                    
# ! error in pak subprocess
# Caused by error: 
# ! Could not solve package dependencies:
# * curl: ! pkgdepends resolution error for curl.
# Caused by error: 
# ! package must be a character vector without NAs
# Type .Last.error to see the more details.
```

There is something in the `local` repo that causes the dependency resolution to fail. I trial-and-error narrowed it down to just these two packages, but can't tell why.
```
Package: curl
Version: 3.3
Depends: R (>= 3.0.0)

Repro from pkgdepends:

options(repos = c(

))

title: Helper function to determine if a package can be added for free?
description:
Hello! I really love this package, so firstly thanks for making something that brings me a little joy every day.

So, I recently used the neat dependency checkers in `pak` to determine if a dependency could be added for free, which was really handy, and I was wondering if something like this might be useful for other users of `pak`?

Here's a little demo for geotargets to help us determine if we could add `withr` or `fs` for free:

``` r
# on master/main branch
can_we_add_a_dep_for_free <- function(deps){
    
    local_deps <- pak::pkg_deps(".")
    
    are_deps_already_free <- deps %in% local_deps$ref
    
    names(are_deps_already_free) <- deps
    
    if (are_deps_already_free) {
        cli::cli_inform(
            message = c(
                "{.pkg {deps}} can be added for free:",
                "Explanation:")
        )
        print(pak::local_deps_explain(deps = deps))
    }
    
    if (!are_deps_already_free){
        cli::cli_inform(
            message = c(
                "{.pkg {deps}} can not be added for free :("
            )
        )
    }
    
}

can_we_add_a_dep_for_free("withr")
#> ℹ Loading metadata database
#> ✔ Loading metadata database ... done
#> 
#> withr can be added for free:
#> Explanation:
#> geotargets -> targets -> tidyselect -> withr
can_we_add_a_dep_for_free("fs")
#> fs can not be added for free :(
```

title: Auth: `Aborted setting keyring password` error in pak when also using the `keyring` package on Linux
description:
I was testing compatibility between `pak` and a separately installed `keyring` package on each OS, and found Windows/macOS to work perfectly. You can set credentials using `keyring` and retrieve/override them with `pak`, and vice-versa. 

I am getting errors trying the same on Linux though, with Ubuntu and the file backend. It looks like pak may be trying to prompt for a keyring password but something goes wrong?

I have not tested the secret service backend because the Gnome Keyring docs are just totally confusing on how you actually run it IMO 😅 

Here are repro steps with docker. If there are issues with docker here, I did also repro the issue on my Ubuntu 22 host.

```sh
# R 4.4, Ubuntu 24
docker run -it --rm rstudio/r-base:4.4-noble bash

# Install nightly pak
R -e 'install.packages("pak", repos = sprintf(
  "https://r-lib.github.io/p/pak/devel/%s/%s/%s",
  .Platform$pkgType,
  R.Version()$os,
  R.Version()$arch
))'

R
```
```r
pak::pkg_install("keyring")

keyring::key_set_with_value("http://localhost", username = "user", password = "pass")
# The 'system' keyring does not exist, enter a keyring password to create it:  
# 🔑 <I just hit enter here>
#  OK
keyring::key_get("http://localhost", username = "user")
# pass

pak::repo_auth_key_get("http://localhost", username = "user")
# Error: 
# ! error in pak subprocess
# Caused by error in `b__file_set_keyring_pass(self, private, key, keyring)`:
# ! Aborted setting keyring password
# Type .Last.error to see the more details.

pak::repo_auth_key_set("http://localhost", username = "user", password = "pass")
# Error: 
# ! error in pak subprocess
# Caused by error in `b__file_set_keyring_pass(self, private, key, keyring)`:
# ! Aborted setting keyring password
# Type .Last.error to see the more details.
```

And if I redo this without using `keyring`, pak works fine:
```r
pak::repo_auth_key_set("http://localhost", username = "user", password = "pass")
pak::repo_auth_key_get("http://localhost", username = "user")
# pass
```

title: conflicting remotes set for packages installed from r-universe via url
description:
Originally from https://github.com/rstudio/renv/issues/2060.

Try installing `cmdstanr` with:

```r
pak::pak(pkg = 'cmdstanr=url::https://stan-dev.r-universe.dev/src/contrib/cmdstanr_0.8.1.tar.gz')
```

The installed package will have the following remotes set:

```r
RemoteUrl: https://github.com/stan-dev/cmdstanr
RemoteRef: v0.8.1
RemoteSha: 02259ef7aa2a8b1c8de2fa3fc42a9feafd789288

The top set of remotes are set on the source package by r-universe; the bottom set are added by `pak`.

title: Support ':' as a sub-directory separator?
description:
`renv` uses `:` in remote specifications, for indicating a sub-directory within a repository. For example:

```r
renv::install("jashapiro/nestedpak:mypak")
```

This doesn't work with `pak`, as a final `/` is instead expected. Would it be possible for `pak` to support this notation as well?

For context, `renv` chose to use `:` here to avoid ambiguity with things like GitLab where repositories could be nested, so `:` allows us to disambiguate whether we're trying to refer to a sub-repository as opposed to a folder within the repository.

Associated issue: https://github.com/rstudio/renv/issues/2011

title: Download only subdirectory for GitHub packages when appropriate
description:
When installing a package from GitHub where the package is in a subdirectory of the main repository, `pak::pkg_install()` downloads the entire repository. For some repositories this may be a non-issue, but if the repository is large (and the R package is only a small part of the repository), this may result in a long, slow download.

Might it be possible to implement a sparse-checkout or equivalent to reduce downloads and improve install times in this situation?

title: keep source without recompiling ?
description:
I would love to be able to see original formatting and comments for every package I install.
