title: Add version control a-la groundhog
description:
Following up on email exchange with Gabor.

I wanted to propose incorporating into 'pak' the type of version control (as an option perhaps) used by the CRAN package _groundhog_.

In groundhog you call groundhog.library(pkg,date), instead of library(pkg), and you install if needed, and then make locally available, the version of the package an all dependencies as available on that date on CRAN (the latest releast available in any format that day). 

So you don't explicitly install packages, they are installed if necessary. 

When installing, groundhog looks for binaries on CRAN, then MRAN, and then source if not available.  But it looks for the binary of the exact version needed only, it does not settle for another version in binary.

Same for all dependencies. 

When a package version is installed, it does not replace an existing version, it is installed on its won version-designated folder, so when using a newever version of a package for a script, you don't risk making previous scripts no longer work, older scripts will continue loading the same older versions.

If within the same R session, the same package is called with different dates that imply different versions, groundhog stops the loading and asks users to eitehr restart the session or choose a compatible date.

This is obviously somewhat similar to renv in goals, but attained in a different way that does not seem would be too difficult to incorporate as optional functionality into 'pak'

It has a few advantages over 'renv', for those uses, including that version control is human-readable instead of hidden as supporting files, and thus also version control does not require additional files. It does not require that users implement their scripts within a version control environment, e.g., github project, the way 'renv' nearly requires.  As the maintainer of renv stated to me: '_The primary mode for collaboration with renv is "use a project directory, and find a way to share that directory with others.'_
That is a great solution for many use cases, but it is not a good solution for many others (e.g., sharing R scripts that support a published research paper).

In terms of the current ability by 'pak' and a few other packages of installing a specific version of the package, this is in my mind inferior to groundhog for a few reasons, including that (1) the version of a package served by MRAN depends on the operating system and R version being used to do the install, so version control is imperfect (the same script does different things on different computers) (2) the new install replaces existing packages (it does not in groundhog), (3) the package needs to be re-installed every time it is used in a different script to ensure the correct version is being used (groundhog stores alternative versions locally side by side).

Groundhog works well with CRAN, and may include github and gitlab packages soon, but I personally would prefer if another mainstream package incorporated the approach and made groundhog redundant.

This is a pitch. If there is any interest, i am happy to discuss further.

title: should pkg_install() accept multiple library paths?
description:
The motivation here would be so that `pak::pkg_install()` only installs packages that are necessary, in case compatible packages are already available in a separate library path. For example:

```
library(pak)
pak::pkg_install("rlang")
.libPaths(c(tempdir(), .libPaths()))
pak::pkg_install("rlang")
```

I see:

```
> library(pak)
> pak::pkg_install("rlang")
✓ Loading metadata database ... done
                                                                           
→ Will update 1 package.
→ The package (861.66 kB) is cached.
+ rlang 0.99.0.9001 → 0.4.12 👷🏾‍♂️🔧

! rlang is loaded in the current R session, you probably need to restart R
after the installation.

? Do you want to continue (Y/n) y
ℹ No downloads are needed, 1 pkg (861.66 kB) is cached
ℹ Building rlang 0.4.12
✓ Built rlang 0.4.12 (2.7s)                                  
✓ Installed rlang 0.4.12  (28ms)                               
✓ 1 pkg: upd 1 [6.4s]                                          
> .libPaths(c(tempdir(), .libPaths()))
> pak::pkg_install("rlang")
 
→ Will install 1 package.
→ The package (861.66 kB) is cached.
+ rlang   0.4.12 👷🏽‍♂️🔧
ℹ No downloads are needed, 1 pkg (861.66 kB) is cached
ℹ Building rlang 0.4.12
✓ Built rlang 0.4.12 (2.9s)                                  
✓ Installed rlang 0.4.12  (18ms)                               
✓ 1 pkg: added 1 [3.1s]   
```

My expectation was that `pak::pkg_install()` would've seen the installation of `rlang` within the other library path, and skipped installation here.

When I try to install a lockfile that is not located in the working directory e.g.

```
lockfile_install(lockfile = "my_dir/pkg.lock")
```

I get the following error:

```
Error: cannot open the connection

```

The installation works fine when the "pkg.lock" file is in my working directory.

I have tried with the new CRAN release and the current dev version on GitHub, but I get the same error with both of them.

Is this expected behavior?  Sorry if I am missing something obvious.

title: pak message use of `>` seems backward
description:
```
pak::pkg_install("milesmcbain/capsule")

v Updating metadata database ... done
 
> Will update 2 packages.
> Will download 2 packages with unknown size.

+ renv    0.13.2     > 0.13.2-102 [bld][cmp][dl] (GitHub: f1dde0e)
```

**Greedy pacman always faces the biggest number** so why is he facing ` 0.1.1.9000` instead of ` 0.3.0.9000`?

I am guessing what's happened here is that `>` is a symbol fallback for a rightward arrow? In the context of package version numbers I have very strong priors for it to be a greater than symbol. It took me a bit to realise this probably wasn't broken.

title: [Feature Request] Easier bundling of packages
description:
This is a niche feature I've always wanted.  It might not fit with the goals of `pak`, but worth a try.

I often want to have students in a class/workshop install a bunch of prep packages, and use them in various projects.  It'd be cool to have a shortcut for bundling, like

```
pak::install_bundle("kbodwin/Stat_331")
library(Stat_331)
```

It's not super different from listing packages individually, but it'd be convenient to update and cleaner in the RMarkdown chunk.

Obviously I could achieve this by making a skeleton -verse package, putting it on GitHub, and having the students install it.  I'm just lazy and want an easy shortcut for that process.

title: Error listing dev dependencies from `Config/Needs/*`
description:
I've run into a puzzling error where the pak isn't recognizing the ref spec in `Config/Needs/website`. The key is that I'm trying to install a package from an alternate repo, e.g. `gadenbuie/pkgdown` rather than `r-lib/pkgdown`.

Here's a small reprex DESCRIPTION file:

```r

#> Setting deferred event(s) on global environment.
#>   * Execute (and clear) with `withr::deferred_run()`.
#>   * Clear (without executing) with `withr::deferred_clear()`.

desc <- desc::description$new("!new")
desc$set("Package", "demo")
desc$set("Imports", "remotes")
desc$set("Config/Needs/website", "gadenbuie/pkgdown, glue")
desc$write("DESCRIPTION")

cat(brio::read_file("DESCRIPTION"))
#> Package: demo
#> Title: {{ Title }}
#> Version: 1.0.0
#> Authors@R: 
#>     c(person(given = "Jo", family = "Doe", email = "jodoe@dom.ain",
```

title: Should remoteSha be set for installation of CRAN packages?
description:
I noticed that for CRAN packages `remoteSha` takes the package version number.

A downstream effect of this is that CRAN packages get written to `{renv}` lockfiles like this:

```
    "DBI": {
      "Package": "DBI",
      "Version": "1.1.1",
      "Source": "CRAN",
      "Repository": "CRAN",
      "RemoteType": "standard",
      "RemotePkgRef": "DBI",
      "RemoteRef": "DBI",
      "RemoteRepos": "https://cran.rstudio.com",
      "RemotePkgPlatform": "windows",
      "RemoteSha": "1.1.1",
      "Hash": "030aaec5bc6553f35347cbb1e70b1a17"
    },
```

I had some logic to check if lockfiles and libraries are in sync. It threw a warning if version numbers are the same but SHAs are different, including if one SHA was NA and one was set. This threw warnings when a non-pak user checked a lockfile written by a pak user.

I can fix the logic etc. But I wonder if the `remoteSha` field should be used for version numbers at all since these represent different concepts?

title: Allow `pkg_system_requirements()` to accept many packages
description:
If I have a handful of packages to install on GHA, I can map over them and individually call `pkg_system_requirements()` to make sure that I don't miss a requirement. 

```r
# current / slow / but works!
lapply(pkgs, function(pkg) {
  pak::pkg_system_requirements(pkg, execute = TRUE)
})
```

This slows down when I have to execute many of the same system requirement commands over and over.

It would be great if I could provide a vector of packages and `pak` would execute them using unique exec statements.

```r
# Want...
pak::pkg_system_requirements(pkgs, execute = TRUE)
```

title: Resolution progress bar looks bad on Linux?
pkg_system_requirements only reports direct sys reqs and ignores imports
description:
As I noticed in https://github.com/r-lib/actions/issues/370 `local_system_requirments` and `pkg_system_requirements` seem to behave unxepectedly different. `local` recursively reports all system requirements of the package and its dependencies, while `pkg` only reports requirements listed directly in the `DESCRIPTION` of the package. I assume this is a bug?

``` r
pth <- fs::path_temp("testpackage")
usethis::create_package(pth, rstudio = FALSE, check_name = FALSE, fields = list(Imports = "gert"))
#> v Creating ...
setwd(pth)
pak::local_install()
#> i Loading metadata database

pak::local_system_requirements(os = "ubuntu", os_release = "18.04")
```

title: pkg_system_requirements() to handle multiple packages
description:
This can be convenient when dealing with a custom set of extra dependencies, such as 

https://github.com/r-lib/actions/blob/a39aa4f7b6750083ec331d4037cc6d6af595c3d9/setup-r-dependencies/action.yaml#L54-L57

title: Move `master` branch to `main`
description:
The `master` branch of this repository will soon be renamed to `main`, as part of a coordinated change across several GitHub organizations (including, but not limited to: [tidyverse](https://github.com/tidyverse), [r-lib](https://github.com/r-lib), [tidymodels](https://github.com/tidymodels), and [sol-eng](https://github.com/sol-eng)). We anticipate this will happen by the end of September 2021.

That will be preceded by a release of the [usethis package](https://usethis.r-lib.org), which will gain some functionality around detecting and adapting to a renamed default branch. There will also be a blog post at the time of this `master` --> `main` change.

The purpose of this issue is to:

* Help us firm up the list of targetted repositories
* Make sure all maintainers are aware of what's coming
* Give us an issue to close when the job is done
* Give us a place to put advice for collaborators re: how to adapt

*message id: euphoric_snowdog*

title: Installation of rlang fails in GitHub action when trying to install the pkgdown dev version with pak
description:
This is a duplicate of [question on SO](https://stackoverflow.com/q/69553621/17141586?stw=2).

I am using the folowing YAML to [run a GitHub action](https://github.com/nflverse/nflplotR/blob/main/.github/workflows/pkgdown.yaml) that should build and deploy a pkgdown website.

```yaml
on:
  push:
    branches: [main, master]
    tags: ['*']
  workflow_dispatch:

name: pkgdown

jobs:
  pkgdown:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      GITHUB_PAT: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v2

      - uses: r-lib/actions/setup-pandoc@v1

      - uses: r-lib/actions/setup-r@v1
        with:
          use-public-rspm: true

      - uses: r-lib/actions/setup-r-dependencies@v1
        with:
          extra-packages: >
            r-lib/pkgdown
          needs: website

      - name: Deploy package
        run: |
          git config --local user.name "$GITHUB_ACTOR"
          git config --local user.email "$GITHUB_ACTOR@users.noreply.github.com"
          Rscript -e 'pkgdown::deploy_to_branch(new_process = FALSE)'

```

This action worked well and the last time was 8 days ago. But since a few days it is failing in the installation stage of dependencies. I will provide a screenshot of the relevant console output as well as the complete log of the stage where it is failing.

title: Specify extra repos in `pkg_install()`
description:
With base `install.packages()`, it's possible to specify additional repos to search in addition to the ones listed in `options("repos")` with the `repos` argument:

```r
install.packages('correlation', repos = 'https://easystats.r-universe.dev')
```

This is convenient, and I've found also easier to explain to my students and users of my packages. It would be nice to be able to do similarly with `pkg_install()` to add an extra repo to the list at function runtime:

```r
pak::pkg_install('correlation', repos = 'https://easystats.r-universe.dev')
```

title: Support for project package libraries
description:
Project library mode can be turned on via an option. (`options`?)

`ROOT` is the root directory of the current project. In general `ROOT/r-pkgs` is used as the default package library. The dependencies in `ROOT/DESCRIPTION` is used as the list of packages to install/update/etc.

`pkg_install`:
- [x] if called without arguments, it uses the local `DESCRIPTION` file to get the set of desired packages.
- [ ] if called with one or more packages, it installs them to the local library, and (by default) also adds them to the local `DESCRIPTION` file.
- [ ] it should be able to remove superfluous packages from the package library.
- [x] it errors if `DESCRIPTION` is not present.
- [x] it creates `r-pkgs` if it does not exist.

`pkg_status`:
- [x] show project library data by default

`pkg_remove`:
- [ ] removes package from the project library, and also from `DESCRIPOTION` (by default)

`devtools` support:
- [ ] `devtools` sets the library path to the project package library, at `load_all()` or for any function that manipulates the package, e.g. `check`, `test`, etc.
- [ ] it errors out if the project package library does not exist, or incomplete, telling you to call `pkg_install`
- [ ] it checks that the installed versions satisfy the required ones. This might need to go online, though, e.g. to check if a GH version is the latest. So we might need a lighter version of the satisfies function.
- [ ] it removes other project package libraries from the library path.

title: Bundling improvements
description:
- [ ] Support dev dependencies?

Currently a package might show up twice, e.g. processx as a dependency and the `r-lib/processx` from `DESCRIPTION`. The installation of the latter fails, of course.

- [x] Support repair in `pak_setup()`

Currently, we don't try to repair an embedded library. But we should.

title: Build self contained package on `R CMD INSTALL`
description:
* If the package is being installed in `R CMD check`, then it should not embed the dependencies. So `R CMD check` is still fast.
* Otherwise we assume that the user needs a self-contained binary, and `R CMD INSTALL` will embed all dependencies. This happens on CRAN when building the Windows and macOS binaries, for users installing the source package from CRAN, etc.
* On the CI, we'll need to write the workflow specially, so that the testing is done on the self-contained package. Maybe `R CMD INSTALL --install-tests`, and then run the tests on the installed package?

title: Relax constraint that DESCRIPTION must be for a Package
description:
The call to `rprojroot::find_package_root_file()` in `pak::local_*()` functions enforces a strict requirement that the `DESCRIPTION` file includes a `Package:` field.

https://github.com/r-lib/pak/blob/49bcef90aa5a48ef0b822d79cae54203acc8673e/R/local.R#L59

`pak::local_install()` is the [current recommended solution](https://github.com/r-lib/remotes/issues/563) for installing packages from a DESCRIPTION that also respects declared package versions. Unfortunately, renv differentiates between `Project:` and `Package:` DESCRIPTION files, which makes it difficult to use `pak::local_*()`.

Relaxing this requirement by using a call like below could make `pak::local_*()` more broadly useful.

```r
rprojroot::find_root_file(path = root, criterion = "description")
```

title: Filenames can be too long on Windows
description:
We are trying to use pak to install dependencies for shiny in GitHub Actions. One of these dependencies is [bslib](https://github.com/rstudio/bslib/), and it fails to build/install with pak. (https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/pull/3230#issuecomment-749857833)

I think the problem is that some filenames are longer than the max length on typical Windows installations.

I think this is the directory where pak tries to unzip the files:

```
C:\\Users\\RUNNER~1\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\Rtmp4K8oTQ\\file10406c64986/src/contrib/bslib_0.2.3.9000_338b05fc5aa551c0cb62dae2ce73ad8c2ceb8403.tar.gz-tree
```

And inside of that, it wants to write the following file:

```
rstudio-bslib-338b05f/inst/lib/bootstrap-accessibility-plugin/plugins/js/bootstrap-accessibility_1.0.3.min.js
```

It fails on that file: https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/runs/1597854296?check_suite_focus=true#step:10:376

The total length of the combined path is 263 characters, which I believe is longer than the max filename length on Windows.

This isn't exactly a bug in pak, but does mean that pak can't be used for GitHub actions on packages that use bslib. The filename in bslib is pretty long, but not crazily long. We could shorten it, but I suspect that other packages would run into the same problem.

title: Print path to lock file that cannot be opened
description:
At some point I interrupted a running `pak::pkg_install()` and thereafter I occasionally get this error when I try to install a package that was part of the interrupted package install:

```r
pak::pkg_install("usethis")                                               
#> → Will install 1 package.
#> → The package (705.78 kB) is cached.
#> + usethis   2.0.0 
#> ℹ No downloads are needed, 1 pkg (705.78 kB) is cached
#> Error: Cannot open lock file: Permission denied                     
#> Type .Last.error.trace to see where the error occured
```

The lock file is hard to find, and `options(error = recover)` isn't helpful since the error originates in a `callr` call. It would be helpful to print the path to the lock file so that the user can debug and/or remove the file.

I was able to use the library path returned from `pak::pak_sitrep()`

```r
pak::pak_sitrep()
#> * pak version:
#> - 0.1.2.9001
#> * Version information:
#> - pak platform: x86_64-apple-darwin17.0 (current: x86_64-apple-darwin17.0, compatible)
#> - pak sha: 1e7825d149591ac548169c4a56dc18b214189da2
#> * Optional packages installed:
#> - tibble
#> * Library path:
#> - /Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/4.0/Resources/library
#> * Private library is embedded.
```

to find (and delete) the `usethis.lock` file.

```r
fs::dir_ls(
  "/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/4.0/Resources/library", 
  recurse = TRUE,
  regexp = "usethis.+lock$"
)
#> /Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/4.0/Resources/library/_cache/usethis.lock
fs::file_delete(.Last.value)
```

After removing the bad lock file, `usethis` installed cleanly.

```r
pak::pkg_install("usethis")                                     
#> → Will install 1 package.
#> → The package (705.78 kB) is cached.
#> + usethis   2.0.0 
#> ℹ No downloads are needed, 1 pkg (705.78 kB) is cached
```

title: Magic `pak()` function
description:
* Only works interactively. 
* Automatically detects if you are developing a package / project / etc. 
* Shows the status of your library / package / project.
* Offers some actions to do, depending on the status.
* Has one argument, which is a ref or list of refs, to install or update and/or add to the package.

## If the current directory is not in a package

Status:
- pak version, whether there is an update (?).
- Summary of libraries (?).
- Cache summary (?).
- Summary of main (first) library.
- Packages that can be updated in the main library.

Actions:
- Update all packages.
- List all packages.

## If the current directory is in a package

- pak version, whether there is an update (?).
- Dependency tree of the package, first level only, annotated.
- Whether the local package is up to date in the main library.
- Dependencies that are missing from the main library.
- Dependencies that are outdated in the main library.
- Summary of "extra" packages, that are not needed for the local package.
- Potential version conflicts of dependencies.

Actions:
- Install/update package.
- Install/update dependencies.
- Install/update dev-dependencies.

title: A Windows story
description:
Recounting what just happened to me on my Windows VM. Perhaps there's something useful in here re: user behaviour.

Overall goal was to install the dev version of googledrive. I deliberately leave my R setup on Windows in a rather primitive state in order to experience how lots of people live.

Successful call to `usethis::create_from_github("tidyverse/googledrive")`.

Immediately try to check. Fail because don't have dev deps. Use `install.packages("devtools")`to make sure devtools is installed and current. Successful.

`devtools::install_dev_deps()`. Get the menu re: "these packages have more recent version available". I say "update all".  These  are all upgrades of CRAN packages.

All succeed except backports. Get the dreaded "cannot remove prior installation" message.

I install pak from CRAN. That works. I attempt both `pak::pkg_install("backports", upgrade = TRUE)` and `pak::pkg_install("backports")`. Both fail in same way.

![backport-failure](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/599454/56844426-d751ee80-6864-11e9-91ea-c6396d836ddc.PNG)

Here is the actual screwed up state of backports:

![backports-library-situation](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/599454/56844433-eafd5500-6864-11e9-9cc7-3d2d07883f6d.PNG)

This dll is the **only** file that exists (deep) below the backports directory in my library.

Perhaps the lesson here is that, had I used pak from the start, I would never have ended up in this [splinched state](https://harrypotter.fandom.com/wiki/Splinching). And I can sort it out. Consider this a report from the field in case pak can help people recover from this sort of dysfunctional initial state.

title: `callr` error on install
description:
Installing using `pak` inside a docker container fails with error `Error: callr subprocess failed: Failed to download abind from 'https://demo.rstudiopm.com/cran/__linux__/bionic/latest/src/contrib/abind_1.4-5.tar.gz'.` The link is valid for the correct tarball.

Installing using `utils::install.packages` works fine. 

Dockerfile below reproduces.

```
# Setup --------
FROM ubuntu:bionic

ARG R_VERSION=3.6.1
ARG R_REPO='https://demo.rstudiopm.com/cran/__linux__/bionic/latest'

# Install R -------------------------------------------------------------------#

RUN apt-get update -y && \
    DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y \
    curl \
    gdebi

RUN curl -O https://cdn.rstudio.com/r/ubuntu-1804/pkgs/r-${R_VERSION}_1_amd64.deb && \
    DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive gdebi --non-interactive r-${R_VERSION}_1_amd64.deb

RUN ln -s /opt/R/${R_VERSION}/bin/R /usr/local/bin/R && \
    ln -s /opt/R/${R_VERSION}/bin/Rscript /usr/local/bin/Rscript

RUN echo "options(\"repos\" = c(RSPM = \"${R_REPO}\"), \"HTTPUserAgent\" = \"R/${R_VERSION} R (${R_VERSION} x86_64-pc-linux-gnu x86_64-pc-linux-gnu x86_64-pc-linux-gnu)\");" >> \
	/opt/R/${R_VERSION}/lib/R/etc/Rprofile.site

# works
RUN /opt/R/${R_VERSION}/bin/R -e "utils::install.packages('pak')"
# fails
RUN /opt/R/${R_VERSION}/bin/R -e "pak::pkg_install('abind')"
# works
RUN /opt/R/${R_VERSION}/bin/R -e "utils::install.packages('abind')"
```

title: upgrade a github package only by its name
description:
I just stumble on behavior I was not expecting from experiences with remotes.

With `remotes` we can do 
```r
remotes::update_packages("chromote")
```
and it will update a github package if this is the one installed, without explicitly providing `rstudio/chromote`

With `pak`, 
```r
pak::pkg_install("chromote", upgrade = T)
```
does not offer to update the package says nothing about the package. 

However, 
```r
pak::pkg_install("rstudio/chromote", upgrade = T)
```

If this behavior to be explicit differs from `remotes` on purpose, there is nothing here and this can be closed.

title: Helper for migrating pkgs across R versions
description:
This has been a question a number of different times, some I can recall are @jennybc's workshop at RStudio::conf, @OmaymaS on twitter (https://twitter.com/OmaymaS_/status/1004468608028807170) and elsewhere.

The general consensus is that typically people take the time to re-build their library from scratch, but this is somewhat painful in practice.

Copying packages directly across R versions is problematic, and enumerating across all R packages in the old library is both tricky (due to GH packages + recommended packages) and often overkill.

One potentially useful way to do this would be to copy only packages which had an OS access time less than a cutoff (maybe 30 days by default), which would let you copy all packages that have been recently in use. We could use the RemoteSHA information in the DESCRIPTION to retrieve GH packages as needed.

This would let you fairly easily re-build the useful set of packages from an old library with one call, and take away a lot of the pain when upgrading to a new R version.

title: Message if R version is outdated
description: Ideally, it would only warn if a binary installer is available for the platform, and only once per session. It probably should not warn on the CIs, and in Docker.

title: Give warnings when library contains packages built with a different major or minor version of R
description:
There are many strange bugs that can happen when you load a package built on a different major or minor version of R. We've spent a lot of time remotely debugging these problems for users and eventually I wrote an article about it. http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/upgrade-R.html

It would be best if `library()` would automatically warn when loading a package like this, but we can't change that directly, so pkgman seems like a reasonable place to do this check. If you think this should go elsewhere, please let me know.

cc: @schloerke, @alandipert, @tmastny. (Today this group spent hours tracking down a crash that was probably due packages built on an old version of R.)

offline use of pak ?
description:
is `pak` suppose to only work in online environment ? 

In our RStudio Server Pro cluster, we are in offline environment and packages can be installed because we are connected an internal CRAN mirror. 

However, `pak` seems to use other source of information for medatada and it throws an error 
```r
> pak::pkg_install("glue")
ℹ Checking for package metadata updates
✖ Metadata download failed                                                                                
Erreur : Failed to connect to 2606:4700:30::681b:bf5c: Le réseau n'est pas accessible     
```

After some search inside code source, I believe this is because by default `pkgcache` use `bioc = TRUE` and use bioc url I can't reached. 

I know that is because bioc repos are supported out of the box by `pak`, but I did not found a way to deactivate the use of bioc repos. 

So at the end, 

* Is there already a way I did not found to activate an offline mode for pak through an option ? 
* Can we try work on something that would allow it ? 

Otherwise, `pak` won't be able to be used on offline environment environment, which is common in some company. 

I'll try for now to see if creating a `pkgcache` medatada, without bioc before using pak, is possible and does the trick

Thanks.

title: Better subprocess control
description:
After #57. 

Since we are only running the subprocess synchronously currently, we can do a better job managing the subprocess. In particular:

- If it is busy at the beginning of the call, kill it and restart it. It should not be busy.
- If it is starting at beginning of the call, wait for it, with a timeout.
- If it is busy at the end of the call (in `on.exit`), kill it and restart it. It should not be busy at this point. (Maybe we could try to interrupt is first, with a very small timeout.)

title: pak 0.11.2 binary for R 4.3 on macOS arm64 can't load curl.so with R 4.3.1: `Symbol not found: _iconv`
description:
The pre-built pak 0.11.2 binary for R 4.3 on macOS arm64 fails to load its bundled `curl.so` on R 4.3.1. pak 0.11.1 worked on the same R. This breaks `r-lib/actions/setup-r-dependencies@v2` for any workflow that tests R 4.3.1 on a macOS arm64 runner.

* Check out the successful workflow run [here](https://github.com/Sage-Bionetworks/synapser/actions/runs/42255073976/job/128019996060)
In the log I could see this is using `v0.11.1`: 
````
> if ("stable" == "repo") { install.packages("pak", lib = Sys.getenv("R_LIB_FOR_PAK")) } else { install.packages("pak", lib = Sys.getenv("R_LIB_FOR_PAK"), repos = sprintf("https://r-lib.github.io/p/pak/%s/%s/%s/%s", "stable", .Platform$pkgType, R.Version()$os, R.Version()$arch)) }
    trying URL '[https://r-lib.github.io/p/pak/stable/mac.binary.big-sur-arm64/darwin20/aarch64/bin/macosx/big-sur-arm64/contrib/4.3/../../../../../../../../darwin20/aarch64/pak_0.11.1_R-4-3_aarch64-darwin20.tgz](https://r-lib.github.io/p/pak/stable/darwin20/aarch64/pak_0.11.1_R-4-3_aarch64-darwin20.tgz)'
    Content type 'application/octet-stream' length 7402335 bytes (7.1 MB)
````

* Checkout the error run [here](https://github.com/Sage-Bionetworks/synapser/actions/runs/42663674105/job/129321540347). This is using `v0.11.2` version of `pak`: 
```
> dir.create(Sys.getenv("R_LIB_FOR_PAK"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
    > 
    > 
    > if ("stable" == "repo") { install.packages("pak", lib = Sys.getenv("R_LIB_FOR_PAK")) } else { install.packages("pak", lib = Sys.getenv("R_LIB_FOR_PAK"), repos = sprintf("https://r-lib.github.io/p/pak/%s/%s/%s/%s", "stable", .Platform$pkgType, R.Version()$os, R.Version()$arch)) }
    trying URL '[https://r-lib.github.io/p/pak/stable/mac.binary.big-sur-arm64/darwin20/aarch64/bin/macosx/big-sur-arm64/contrib/4.3/../../../../../../../../darwin20/aarch64/pak_0.11.2_R-4-3_aarch64-darwin20.tgz](https://r-lib.github.io/p/pak/stable/darwin20/aarch64/pak_0.11.2_R-4-3_aarch64-darwin20.tgz)'

```
We saw error in the `Repo Status`: 
```
    Error: 
    ! error in pak subprocess
    Caused by error in `dyn.load(file, DLLpath = DLLpath, ...)`:
    ! unable to load shared object '/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/4.3-arm64/Resources/site-library/pak/library/curl/libs/curl.so':
      dlopen(/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/4.3-arm64/Resources/site-library/pak/library/curl/libs/curl.so, 0x0006): Symbol not found: _iconv
      Referenced from: <8A5AA830-E424-36FE-B576-17CCA4056CEC> /Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/4.3-arm64/Resources/site-library/pak/library/curl/libs/curl.so
      Expected in:     <E727677E-6116-3B73-A86B-E3AB4DFB621A> /Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/4.3-arm64/Resources/lib/libR.dylib
    ---
    Backtrace:
    1. pak::repo_status()
    2. pak:::remote(function(...) asNamespace("pak")$repo_status_internal(...), …
    3. err$throw(res$error)
```

## Environment

- GitHub Actions `macos-15-arm64`
- R 4.3.1, the official CRAN arm64 build, installed by `r-lib/actions/setup-r@v2`
- pak installed by `r-lib/actions/setup-r-dependencies@v2` (`pak-version: stable`)
  which downloads `pak_0.11.2_R-4-3_aarch64-darwin20.tgz`

The pak README lists "macOS Big Sur+ / aarch64 / R 4.1.0 - R-devel" as supported, so I expected R 4.3.1 to work.
